carbon_policy_signal.item: COP31 draft text signals immediate fossil fuel transition; methane deal emerging; EU court upholds Poland's 7 climate laws, reinforcing coal phase-out trajectory and EUA structural demand.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Strengthened global climate commitment and EU coal phase-out durability raise long-dated EUA floor and power decarbonization pathway; methane rules tighten upstream gas economics.

freshness_caveat: Coal (326 days old, as of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark (321 days old, as of 2025-12-31) are stale; latest TTF, GB Power, DE Power, Clean Spark, Renewables, Storage, and EUA current as of 2026-11-16–17. Coal and Clean Dark price-dependent analysis unreliable.
risk_flags: Storage 18 pp below 5-yr seasonal average; refill pace through winter will set H1 2027 power risk and TTF curve shape.
GB Power at 91st-percentile (-16.6% daily pullback suggests mean reversion risk); renewable share at 89th-percentile (312.66% weekly swing indicates volatility in thermal dispatch).
EU bans Russian Yamal LNG from 2027 (~5 mtpa); no alternative announced — timing and rerouting logistics will drive TTF forward premium.
TTF outsized daily move (-6.82%, 2.1σ) coincides with LNG ban news; watch for volatility spillover into Cal+1 and calendar spreads.

base.summary: Storage refill proceeds at seasonal pace; LNG rerouting priced into TTF forward; GB power normalizes toward median.

downside.summary: Mild winter, accelerated storage refill, demand softening; Trump policy eases LNG supply uncertainty; thermal dispatch weakens.

upside.summary: Cold front delays storage refill; LNG rerouting logistics confirm higher Atlantic cost; GB supply tightens.

themes: GB power premium sustained by storage tightness and renewables volatility
EU-Russia LNG trade severing; marginal cost of supply shifting to costlier Atlantic/Pacific routes
Coal structural collapse masks firm thermal baseload requirement
COP31 climate framework durability underpins long-term EUA floor
top_drivers: EU bans Russian Yamal LNG from 2027 (~5 mtpa); marginal rerouting to Atlantic/Pacific costlier routes lifts TTF forward curve and power fuel cost.
Storage 18 pp below 5-yr seasonal; tight winter refill pace forces thermal dispatch reliance and sustains GB Power premium (91st-percentile).
Coal at 8th-percentile historically low offsets firm baseload need; thermal merit order recalibration on renewables volatility (89th-percentile, 312% weekly swing).
top_takeaway: GB Power at 91st-percentile amid tight storage (-18 pp seasonal) offsets collapsing coal (8th-percentile); EU bans Russian LNG from 2027, raising TTF forward curve via Atlantic/Pacific rerouting.

watchlist.metric: EU 2027 Russian LNG ban enforcement & spot LNG procurement
watchlist.why: Loss of ~5 mtpa forces marginal sourcing from Atlantic/Pacific at higher cost; TTF forward curve repricing horizon is 12–24 months.

watchlist.metric: COP31 final fossil fuel transition text & methane rules
watchlist.why: EUA floor expectations and gas cost risk premium locked into final language; could shift power merit order and storage withdrawal strategy.

watchlist.metric: EU Storage refill trajectory through Dec–Jan
watchlist.why: Currently 18 pp below seasonal; slow refill or demand surge would force gas-to-coal switch, lifting both TTF and thermal spreads into spring.
US LNG export licensing and sanctions posture unresolved; risk to Atlantic supply cost assumptions underpinning EU forward curve.

watchlist_dated.name: COP31 final text adoption
watchlist_dated.why: Fossil fuel transition language and methane rules finalization; signals EUA structural demand and gas sector cost pressure.
